verdict.root_cause: At 08:18:53 UTC platform-automation attached a traffic-shaping container to the cart-service network namespace applying a fixed 300ms, zero-jitter delay on eth0 egress (tr_0a41300a4f4b). Because the rule applies to the whole pod namespace, every outbound cartservice call — in practice its Redis cache round-trips — pays a constant ~300ms penalty. Traces confirm the mechanism exactly: HGET and HMSET spans alike cluster in a tight 300-310ms band with negligible cartservice self-time, and the per-request penalty scales with cache-call count (single-op GetCart/EmptyCart ~301-309ms, two-op AddItem ~603-611ms), while non-cart paths (productcatalog, currency, payment, shipping, email, messaging) stay sub-millisecond to ~20ms in the same window (tr_b168907e2864). cartservice never errored or crashed — its logs show continuous normal cart operations on both sides of the incident (tr_3f1fe3ae621b) — it simply became slow. Callers absorbed the wait: checkoutservice's intra-request step latency grew roughly 50x between the head and tail of the window while still completing orders with gap-free topic offsets (tr_d18393976354), and its error ratio rose from a zero baseline to a ~7.9% peak (tr_4ee611489716), the partial-failure signature of a degraded, not absent, dependency. The failing mechanism is injected wait on a dependency call path, not a wrong artifact and not a wrong configuration value being consumed by the application.
verdict.reasoning: Three independent lines converge. (1) A discrete, timestamped trigger exists 3.6 minutes before the incident marker: a network-layer 300ms fixed-delay shaping rule attached to cartservice's namespace, with no deploy, image change, flag flip, or cache-side change recorded in the same window (tr_0a41300a4f4b). (2) The trace shape matches that trigger's signature precisely rather than merely correlating with it — uniform magnitude across read and write commands, near-zero variance, no tail, and additive scaling with the number of cache calls per request; cartservice compute, GC and a cluster-wide mesh fault are each excluded by the same span data (tr_b168907e2864). (3) The blast pattern is exactly a latency, not an error, propagation: cartservice logs stay clean and the process never dies (tr_3f1fe3ae621b), while callers show wall-clock inflation first (tr_d18393976354) and only a partial ~7.9% error fraction second (tr_4ee611489716), consistent with upstream timeouts firing on a slow-but-alive dependency. I deliberately did not classify this as bad_config despite a configuration act upstream: the shaping rule is not a value the application reads and misuses, it is a delay inserted into the call path, and the wait itself is what breaks the requests. The past cart-redis-misconfig and cart-bad-image-tag incidents both featured cartservice showing flat-zero errors while being the true origin, and cartservice's error-rate query here returned no series at all (tr_4f3c96261fcf) — a null, not a zero. That trap is noted but does not change the verdict, because the trace evidence gives a positive mechanism rather than an inference from cart's apparent health. Remediation is removal of the injected shaping rule (detach the traffic-shaping container / revert the platform-automation action); a rollback or restart of cartservice would not help, since the running artifact is correct and the delay lives in the pod's network namespace.
open_questions: checkoutservice's client spans for GetCart/EmptyCart exceed the matching cartservice server spans by ~900ms, roughly triple the ~300ms gap seen from frontend (tr_b168907e2864). An additional caller-side factor on the checkout→cart path — connection setup, retries, or queuing — is unexplained and could mean the 300ms injection is being amplified there.

cartservice's error-rate ratio returned no series at all rather than zero (tr_4f3c96261fcf), so it is unknown whether cartservice emitted any error-status calls. This is a label, metric-name or instrumentation-coverage gap that should be resolved before asserting cartservice returned clean.

Both log queries were truncated and returned nothing from roughly 08:20-08:25 (tr_3f1fe3ae621b, tr_d18393976354), so the interval containing the 08:22:30 alert was never read directly. Any timeout or error burst confined to that gap is unobserved.

checkoutservice's ~7.9% error peak is aggregated by service_name only, with no per-peer breakdown (tr_4ee611489716). Whether those errors are all cart-path timeouts, or include independent payment/shipping/email failures, is not established.

Whether the traffic-shaping rule is still attached at query time, and whether it was an intentional chaos experiment with a scheduled teardown or an unintended action, is not settled by the change record.

No pre-08:18:53 cartservice spans were returned (tr_b168907e2864), so the healthy baseline for cache round-trip latency is inferred from unaffected peer services rather than measured on the cart path itself.
